tagline: A lane and a half of gravel across high desert.
intro: East of Jordan Valley, Oregon, the Mud Flat Road follows Jordan Creek past hay meadows and lone ranches, then climbs through juniper and mahogany. Fifteen miles out the pavement ends. The next 74 miles are gravel, across rim-rocked plateaus of sagebrush and bunchgrass cut by the canyons of the Owyhee River.

Jordan Valley began as a supply depot for the Owyhee mines after gold turned up on Jordan Creek in 1863. Near the far end the road crosses a saddle at 6,133 feet, comes down the Poison Creek drainage among willows and cottonwoods, and crosses salt desert to Idaho 78 near Grand View.
season: Visit Idaho gives early summer and fall as the best times to drive it.

moments.title: North Fork Owyhee River
moments.text: The road drops from a rim of stunted old-growth juniper into the canyon of the North Fork, where the BLM keeps a primitive campground.

moments.title: Al Perry Bluebird Trail
moments.text: Between Nickel Creek and Pleasant Valley white nest boxes stand on posts beside the road for the mountain bluebird, 25 of them in 1977 and 370 by 1991.

moments.title: Turmes Ranch
moments.text: The Turmes family settled here in 1880, planted an orchard, kept a way station for travelers for many years, and left the stone buildings that still stand.

practical: The byway is mostly gravel, about a lane and a half wide, with no services between Jordan Valley and Grand View. It is usually impassable from late November through March, and rain can make it slick.
